Subject: Dedicated capacity - integration & autoscaling follow-up

Hi Sara / Michael —

Thanks again for the conversation earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Recap (from our discovery):
- Primary workload: user-facing document summarization + multi-stage reranking for search. Expected steady-state qps: ~120 requests/sec during business hours with 4x spikes for peak processing windows.
- Latency SLO: p95 generation < 300ms for single-turn summaries; re-ranker/embeddings calls can be async but need end-to-end < 1s for search flows.
- Security: VPC peering preferred; keys via customer KMS.
- Compliance: SOC2 + audit log retention for 12 months required.

Integration items we agreed to validate:
1) SDK setup & auth — sample SDK flow, support for token-based and mTLS/KMS key signing (we suggest Customer KMS + Redwood-managed key wrap).
2) Routing & model variants — can route by region and fallback to a smaller quantized variant for capacity constraints.
3) Structured output/tool calling — your pipeline calls an extract->rerank->generate flow; we'll provide tool-calling hooks + structured JSON output via function-calling to simplify parsing.
4) Embeddings & rerankers — propose dedicated embedding nodes with batched commits; discuss vector DB integration (we recommended client-side Faiss vs Redwood-managed embedding cache).
5) Autoscaling & queue sizing — baseline capacity for steady qps, burst pool for 4x spikes, and a backpressure queue to preserve p95 tail behavior.

Action items / proposed owners:
- Redwood: provide a short integration guide + sample SDK repo with auth examples (Aditya) — ETA Nov 20.
- FinCloud: share realistic traffic snapshots and vector DB sizing info (Michael) — ETA Nov 20.
- Joint: whiteboard autoscaling policy and queue thresholds (sync next week).
- Procurement: Sara, loop in procurement contact for early T&Cs and PO process.

Attachments: I attached a short list of architecture questions (redwood-dedicated-arch-questions.pdf) and a mutual action plan template.

Next step: Aditya will follow with a technical note on auth, SDK snippets, and recommended queue/concurrency settings. Can we do a 30-min follow-up on Tue 11/23 to walk the tech team through the SDK + autoscaling proposal?

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Michael — great context, thanks for the traffic sample. Quick answers and a proposed default config you can iterate on: 

Auth & SDK:
- We support token-based, mTLS, and KMS-integrated signing. For Private (VPC) deployments we typically recommend mTLS for mutual endpoint authentication + KMS for encryption-at-rest of keys.
- I'll attach a short SDK snippet in the repo we promised; it demonstrates mTLS handshake and token refresh logic.

Embeddings:
- We can expose a dedicated embedding service with batching size tunable per tenant. For 10M vectors, we recommend client-side periodically flushing batches >= 256 vectors for throughput efficiency. Redwood can write to Milvus via a secure connector or you can push vectors to your DB.

Autoscaling & Queueing (proposed starting config):
- Baseline: enough GPU-backed serving nodes to handle 150 rps with p95 headroom.
- Burst pool: additional warm capacity that can be evicted/freed after 60s of low utilization; configured to cover 4x spikes up to 600 rps for short windows.
- Concurrency limits: per-request concurrency limit on generation calls set to 8 per worker process; overall shard concurrency tuned based on model latency profiles.
- Queue policy: per-tenant FIFO queue with token-bucket smoothing. Timeouts: default request TTL 10s (configurable). Under sustained overload we apply adaptive shedding: lower-priority/async requests are queued longer; we return explicit 429 with retry-after for requests that exceed queue TTL.

Sizing note: since your p95 target is tight (<300ms) we recommend smaller batch sizes for generation (to keep latency) and larger batch windows for embedding commits (throughput). We'll provide an empirical matrix once we run a short load test.

Next steps:
- I'll push the SDK repo + sample mTLS keys and an integration guide to the HubSpot doc link by EOW (Nov 20).
- Can we get a quick runbook from FinCloud with their preferred vector ingestion pattern so we can recommend connector vs push?
